title: Non-Linearities and Their Local Gradients
summary: Why networks need non-linearities, how ReLU, GELU and softmax work, how each passes gradients backward, and the max-subtraction trick that keeps softmax from overflowing.
takeaways: Without non-linearities, stacked layers collapse into one linear map.
Backprop multiplies the upstream gradient by each function's local derivative.
ReLU gates gradients: they pass where x > 0 and are zeroed elsewhere.
Always compute softmax as softmax(x − max(x)). It's mathematically identical and never overflows.

steps.label: Forward
steps.detail: Compute a = f(x) and keep x (or a) for the backward pass.

steps.label: Upstream gradient
steps.detail: Receive dout = ∂L/∂a from the next layer.

steps.label: Pass it on
steps.detail: Send dx to the previous layer and repeat.
